Need to search first.I don't have any notes on Proverbs 23 for you yet, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

My first attempt to open the commentary pages was blocked: the fetch tool only opens a page after it has turned up in a search, and I went straight to the URLs. When I then tried to run the searches, the system told me I had used up my tool calls for this turn. I haven't read enduringword.com, biblehub.com, studylight.org, preceptaustin.org or any of the other approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So any verse notes I wrote now would break those rules.

**What I'll do when you resend the request (for example, "continue"):**
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word (Guzik) on Proverbs 23; Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com; studylight.org; preceptaustin.org.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** pages from the tradition-specific sites on the verses most likely to divide them:
   - vv. 13–14: the rod and discipline
   - vv. 20–21 and 29–35: wine, drunkenness and whether Christians should drink at all
   - vv. 4–5: wealth
3. **Other views:** the netbible.org translation notes and bibleodyssey.org (modern scholarship). For vv. 1–11, I'll check whether they mention the Egyptian *Instruction of Amenemope*, but I'll only include it if a page actually says so. Then Catholic and Orthodox sources (newadvent.org, catholic.com, oca.org), and anything the sites say about prosperity teaching in relation to vv. 4–5.

Every point will have its URL, and verses with nothing found will be left out.
